title: Brush Up: The 5-Minute Daily News - AI/Tech, Biz, World
description: Your definitive morning intelligence download. Every day shortly after 7:00 AM EST, we bypass the noise to deliver the critical shifts in AI, Global Business, and Macroeconomics that define the modern landscape. Brush up on the news while you brush up your smile.
latestSummary:
Google’s Gemini app surpasses 750 million monthly active users, intensifying competition in the AI market and fueling speculation about a potential Apple partnership. Andreessen Horowitz invested $1.7 billion in AI infrastructure, including OpenAI and ElevenLabs, further demonstrating confidence in the sector. ElevenLabs’ valuation soared to $11 billion following a $500 million funding round, highlighting the rapid growth in specialized AI. Sam Altman publicly criticized Claude’s Super Bowl ads, reflecting the high stakes in AI market leadership.

KKR and Singtel acquired STT GDC for $5.2 billion, reflecting the growing demand for digital infrastructure. Advanced Micro Devices is betting on its MI450 AI accelerator for future growth. General Motors increased its dividend, signaling financial strength.

Globally, the expiration of the New Start treaty raises concerns about a potential nuclear arms race. The US is implementing a plan to counter China’s dominance in critical minerals. Tensions between the US and China escalated with Xi Jinping’s warning to Trump regarding Taiwan. In Nigeria, escalating violence prompted a US military deployment.

title: Overnight Market Brief - Bridging the Global Gap. Daily.
description:
While North America sleeps, the global economy keeps moving. Overnight Market Brief is your essential pre-market digest, designed for traders, serious investors, and professionals who need to hit the ground running.
Most North American investors miss 50% of the market story because it happens in Tokyo, Hong Kong, and London. We bridge that gap. Every morning at 8:00 AM ET, we deliver a concise, data-driven breakdown and full global picture in under 10 minutes, just in time for your morning commute.
latestSummary:
Wall Street opened defensively on Thursday, February 5, 2026, with the S&P 500 down 0.51% and the Nasdaq 100 declining 1.77%. The session was characterized by a strengthening US Dollar, broader risk aversion, and declining commodity prices, including crude oil and gold. The 10-Year Treasury Yield decreased to 4.258%, while the US Dollar Index rose to 97.63.

Overnight, Asian markets exhibited mixed performance; Tokyo’s Nikkei 225 fell 0.88%, while Greater China saw the Hang Seng rise 0.14% and the Shanghai Composite decline 0.64%. European markets followed a cautious trend, influenced by mixed economic data including a rise in German industrial orders and an easing slump in UK construction.

US futures reflected this cautious sentiment, with S&P 500 futures down 0.67% and Nasdaq 100 futures down 1.02%. Investors are anticipating central bank decisions from the ECB and Bank of England, alongside the Challenger survey’s planned layoffs data and European economic indicators. The market’s path appears to be downward, awaiting developments from these key catalysts.

title: Post-market Recap
description:
Did the market "rally into the close" or "fade the open"? The Post-Market Recap goes beyond the green and red arrows to analyze the structure of the trading day. This daily briefing dissects the inter-market correlations that drove the session.
Every afternoon, we cover:
Macro Causality: Connecting the dots between the 10-Year Yield, the Dollar Index, and Equities.
Tech & AI Pulse: A dedicated segment on the semiconductor ecosystem and Big Tech performance.
Market Breadth: Analyzing Volatility (VIX) and Sector Rotation to gauge genuine institutional sentiment.
Closing Catalysts: Identifying the specific news and data that triggered late-day reversals.
latestSummary:
The Post-Market Recap by AGI Era on February 4, 2026, presented a mixed market day with divergent trends. The Dow Jones Industrial Average gained 260.31 points to close at 49501.30, driven by a rotation into value sectors, while the S&P 500 declined 0.51% to 6882.72 and the Nasdaq 100 fell 1.77% to 24891.24, largely due to technology sector weakness. Trading volume on the S&P 500 was substantial at 3.52 billion shares, suggesting participation but not overwhelming institutional movement.

Sector rotation was a key theme, with the Technology Select Sector SPDR Fund (XLK) lagging significantly, while the Utilities Select Sector SPDR Fund (XLU) demonstrated resilience. This shift indicates a defensive positioning by investors, potentially reflecting concerns about future economic growth and interest rate expectations. The US Dollar Index rose 0.24% to 97.53, likely fueled by rising interest rate expectations. Crude Oil prices increased 1.83% to $64.37, adding to inflationary pressures.

Within the tech sector, Nvidia experienced a notable decline, while Microsoft and Apple showed relative strength. However, declines across the “Magnificent Seven” highlighted investor selectivity and potential re-evaluations of valuations in a higher interest rate environment.  The after-hours movement of Take-Two Interactive (TTWO) was noted, potentially driven by company-specific news. Tomorrow’s trading will focus on the S&P 500’s 6850-6900 range and developments regarding bond yields and the dollar.

title: Geopolitical Updates
description: Beyond the headlines lies strategy. Geopolitical Updates is your daily guide to the evolving global order. Each episode provides a rapid scan of the day's top international stories, followed by a deep-dive analysis of the single most impactful event shifting the geopolitical landscape. From tension in the South China Sea to economic statecraft in Europe, we explain not just what happened today, but why it matters for tomorrow. Delivered daily at 7 PM ET.
latestSummary:
The New Start treaty’s impending expiration is the dominant geopolitical concern tonight, raising fears of a new nuclear arms race between the U.S. and Russia. Without this treaty limiting strategic nuclear warheads, transparency decreases, potentially fueling mistrust and aggressive postures from both nations. Russia’s increased interest in tactical nuclear weapons and the Pentagon’s concerns about novel Russian weapons systems highlight this risk.

Meanwhile, the conflict in Gaza continues with Israeli strikes resulting in civilian casualties, and tensions escalate with an Iranian drone shot down near an American carrier in the Arabian Sea. Economically, a new arms race would significantly increase defense spending for the U.S. and Russia, diverting resources from other sectors.

Internationally, the U.S. and India finalized a trade deal, though experts caution against over-optimism. In Europe, a German activist was jailed in Hungary following a Nazi rally, raising human rights concerns. Finally, Libya remains unstable with an investigation into the death of Muammar Gaddafi’s son. The geopolitical landscape is characterized by escalating tensions and a heightened risk of nuclear escalation.
